WITH pubs AS (
  SELECT
    "publication_date" AS publication_date,
    "publication_number" AS publication_number,
    "country_code" AS country_code,
    "inventor" AS inventor
  FROM PATENTS.PATENTS.PUBLICATIONS
),
inventor_counts AS (
  SELECT
    publication_number,
    country_code,
    publication_date,
    -- count number of inventor entries if inventor is an array/object; handle NULL
    CASE
      WHEN inventor IS NULL THEN 0
      WHEN TYPEOF(inventor) = 'ARRAY' THEN ARRAY_SIZE(inventor)
      WHEN TYPEOF(inventor) = 'OBJECT' THEN 1
      ELSE 1
    END AS inventor_count
  FROM pubs
),
filtered AS (
  SELECT
    publication_number,
    country_code,
    publication_date,
    inventor_count
  FROM inventor_counts
  WHERE inventor_count >= 1
    AND publication_date IS NOT NULL
    AND publication_date BETWEEN 19600101 AND 20201231
    AND country_code = 'CA'
),
buckets AS (
  SELECT
    publication_number,
    inventor_count,
    publication_date,
    -- compute year from YYYYMMDD numeric
    FLOOR(publication_date / 10000) AS year,
    -- compute 5-year bucket start: 1960..2020
    CASE
      WHEN FLOOR(publication_date / 10000) BETWEEN 1960 AND 2020
      THEN (FLOOR((FLOOR(publication_date / 10000) - 1960) / 5) * 5) + 1960
      ELSE NULL
    END AS bucket_start
  FROM filtered
),
agg AS (
  SELECT
    bucket_start,
    COUNT(*) AS total_publications,
    AVG(inventor_count) AS avg_inventors_per_publication
  FROM buckets
  WHERE bucket_start IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY bucket_start
)
SELECT
  CONCAT(bucket_start::TEXT, '-', (bucket_start + 4)::TEXT) AS five_year_period,
  avg_inventors_per_publication,
  total_publications
FROM agg
ORDER BY bucket_start

WITH pubs AS (
  SELECT
    "publication_number" AS publication_number,
    "family_id"            AS family_id,
    "country_code"         AS country_code,
    "publication_date"     AS publication_date,
    "assignee_harmonized"  AS assignee_harmonized,
    "cpc"                  AS cpc
  FROM PATENTS.PATENTS.PUBLICATIONS
),
-- extract CPC symbols array items (assuming cpc is array of objects with 'section' or 'symbol')
cpc_expanded AS (
  SELECT
    publication_number,
    family_id,
    country_code,
    publication_date,
    assignee_harmonized,
    f.value::string AS cpc_symbol
  FROM pubs,
  LATERAL FLATTEN(input => cpc) f
),
-- derive CPC section (first letter of symbol) and filter to section 'A61'
cpc_sectioned AS (
  SELECT
    publication_number,
    family_id,
    country_code,
    publication_date,
    assignee_harmonized,
    CASE
      WHEN cpc_symbol IS NOT NULL THEN UPPER(SUBSTR(cpc_symbol,1,3)) -- try first 3 chars to capture e.g. A61K
      ELSE NULL
    END AS cpc_prefix
  FROM cpc_expanded
),
-- keep only records where any cpc prefix starts with 'A61' (so publication is in category A61)
a61_pubs AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    publication_number,
    family_id,
    country_code,
    publication_date,
    assignee_harmonized
  FROM cpc_sectioned
  WHERE cpc_prefix LIKE 'A61%'
    AND assignee_harmonized IS NOT NULL
),
-- normalize assignee name and compute year from publication_date (assuming publication_date is YYYYMMDD or YYYY as number)
pubs_with_year AS (
  SELECT
    publication_number,
    family_id,
    country_code,
    assignee_harmonized,
    CASE
      WHEN publication_date IS NULL THEN NULL
      WHEN publication_date > 9999 THEN TO_NUMBER(TO_VARCHAR(publication_date)::VARCHAR(10)) / 10000 -- fallback (not used)
      ELSE publication_date
    END AS pub_date_num,
    CASE
      WHEN publication_date IS NULL THEN NULL
      WHEN publication_date >= 10000000 THEN FLOOR(publication_date/10000) -- YYYYMMDD numeric -> YYYY
      WHEN publication_date >= 100000 THEN FLOOR(publication_date/10000) -- other formats
      WHEN publication_date >= 10000 THEN FLOOR(publication_date/10000)
      ELSE publication_date -- if already year
    END AS pub_year
  FROM a61_pubs
),
-- count patents per assignee per year
assignee_year_counts AS (
  SELECT
    assignee_harmonized AS assignee,
    pub_year AS year,
    COUNT(DISTINCT family_id) AS patent_count
  FROM pubs_with_year
  WHERE assignee_harmonized IS NOT NULL
    AND pub_year IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY 1,2
),
-- find busiest year per assignee (max patents)
assignee_busiest_year AS (
  SELECT
    assignee,
    year,
    patent_count,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY assignee ORDER BY patent_count DESC, year ASC) AS rn
  FROM assignee_year_counts
),
-- pick the single most active assignee overall by their busiest-year patent_count
most_active_assignee AS (
  SELECT assignee, year, patent_count
  FROM assignee_busiest_year
  WHERE rn = 1
  ORDER BY patent_count DESC
  LIMIT 1
),
-- for that assignee and year, count filings by jurisdiction (country_code)
jurisdiction_counts AS (
  SELECT
    p.country_code AS country_code,
    COUNT(DISTINCT p.family_id) AS cnt
  FROM pubs_with_year p
  JOIN most_active_assignee m
    ON p.assignee_harmonized = m.assignee
   AND p.pub_year = m.year
  WHERE p.country_code IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY 1
),
-- top 5 jurisdictions
top5 AS (
  SELECT country_code
  FROM jurisdiction_counts
  ORDER BY cnt DESC, country_code
  LIMIT 5
)
SELECT LISTAGG(country_code, ',') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY country_code) AS top_5_jurisdictions
FROM top5

WITH pubs AS (
  SELECT
    "publication_number" AS publication_number,
    "family_id"           AS family_id,
    "publication_date"    AS publication_date,
    "filing_date"         AS filing_date,
    "assignee_harmonized" AS assignee_harmonized,
    "cpc"                 AS cpc
  FROM PATENTS.PATENTS.PUBLICATIONS
),
-- extract CPC symbols (assume cpc is an array/variant of entries with "section" or "symbol" fields; handle common shapes)
pubs_cpc AS (
  SELECT
    publication_number,
    family_id,
    publication_date,
    filing_date,
    assignee_harmonized,
    TRIM(UPPER(value:"symbol"::STRING)) AS symbol,
    TRIM(UPPER(value::STRING)) AS symbol_raw
  FROM pubs,
  LATERAL FLATTEN(input => cpc) f
),
-- filter to CPC entries that start with 'A61'
pubs_a61 AS (
  SELECT
    publication_number,
    family_id,
    COALESCE(filing_date, publication_date) AS event_date,
    assignee_harmonized
  FROM pubs_cpc
  WHERE (symbol IS NOT NULL AND symbol LIKE 'A61%')
     OR (symbol_raw IS NOT NULL AND symbol_raw LIKE 'A61%')
),
-- expand assignee_harmonized (could be array of names or single)
assignees_expanded AS (
  SELECT
    publication_number,
    family_id,
    event_date,
    TRIM(value::STRING) AS assignee
  FROM pubs_a61,
  LATERAL FLATTEN(input => assignee_harmonized) f2
),
-- normalize event year and count applications per assignee per family (count unique application/family to represent applications)
assignee_family AS (
  SELECT
    assignee,
    family_id,
    DATE_PART(year, TO_DATE(event_date::STRING, 'YYYYMMDD')) AS year
  FROM assignees_expanded
  WHERE assignee IS NOT NULL AND event_date IS NOT NULL
),
-- count applications per assignee per year (count distinct families)
counts_per_year AS (
  SELECT
    assignee,
    year,
    COUNT(DISTINCT family_id) AS applications
  FROM assignee_family
  GROUP BY assignee, year
),
-- find assignee with the most total applications (across years)
assignee_totals AS (
  SELECT
    assignee,
    SUM(applications) AS total_applications
  FROM counts_per_year
  GROUP BY assignee
),
top_assignee AS (
  SELECT assignee
  FROM assignee_totals
  ORDER BY total_applications DESC
  LIMIT 1
)
-- for that assignee, find the year with the max applications
SELECT
  c.year,
  c.applications
FROM counts_per_year c
JOIN top_assignee t ON c.assignee = t.assignee
ORDER BY c.applications DESC, c.year ASC
LIMIT 1

WITH pubs AS (
  SELECT
    "publication_number" AS publication_number,
    "application_number" AS application_number,
    "country_code" AS country_code,
    "family_id" AS family_id,
    "application_number_formatted" AS application_number_formatted,
    "filing_date" AS filing_date,
    "publication_date" AS publication_date,
    "assignee_harmonized" AS assignee_harmonized,
    "cpc" AS cpc
  FROM PATENTS.PATENTS.PUBLICATIONS
),
-- explode cpc array/object to get symbols; CPC structure varies, handle arrays of objects with .symbol
pubs_cpc AS (
  SELECT
    publication_number,
    application_number,
    country_code,
    family_id,
    application_number_formatted,
    filing_date,
    publication_date,
    assignee_harmonized,
    TRIM(FLATTEN.value:"symbol"::STRING) AS cpc_symbol
  FROM pubs,
  LATERAL FLATTEN(input => pubs.cpc) AS FLATTEN
),
-- filter for class A01B3 (match prefix)
a01b3 AS (
  SELECT *
  FROM pubs_cpc
  WHERE cpc_symbol IS NOT NULL
    AND UPPER(cpc_symbol) LIKE 'A01B3%' 
),
-- extract assignee name: assignee_harmonized may be array; flatten to get names
assignees AS (
  SELECT
    a01b3.*,
    TRIM(assignee.value:"name"::STRING) AS assignee_name
  FROM a01b3,
  LATERAL FLATTEN(input => a01b3.assignee_harmonized) AS assignee
),
-- derive year (prefer filing_date, fallback to publication_date). Dates are numeric YYYYMMDD or timestamp; extract year by dividing
with_year AS (
  SELECT
    assignee_name,
    application_number,
    country_code,
    CASE
      WHEN filing_date IS NOT NULL AND filing_date != 0 THEN TO_VARCHAR(TRY_TO_NUMBER(TO_CHAR(filing_date))) 
      ELSE NULL
    END AS filing_raw,
    CASE
      WHEN filing_date IS NOT NULL AND filing_date != 0 THEN FLOOR(filing_date/10000)::INT
      WHEN publication_date IS NOT NULL AND publication_date != 0 THEN FLOOR(publication_date/10000)::INT
      ELSE NULL
    END AS year
  FROM assignees
),
-- count total applications per assignee (distinct application_number)
assignee_totals AS (
  SELECT
    assignee_name,
    COUNT(DISTINCT application_number) AS total_applications
  FROM with_year
  WHERE assignee_name IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY assignee_name
),
-- top 3 assignees by total applications
top3 AS (
  SELECT assignee_name, total_applications
  FROM assignee_totals
  ORDER BY total_applications DESC
  LIMIT 3
),
-- for those top3, find year with most applications and counts
yearly_counts AS (
  SELECT
    w.assignee_name,
    w.year,
    COUNT(DISTINCT w.application_number) AS apps_in_year
  FROM with_year w
  JOIN top3 t ON w.assignee_name = t.assignee_name
  WHERE w.year IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY w.assignee_name, w.year
),
-- pick max year per assignee (if tie, choose smallest year)
top_year_per_assignee AS (
  SELECT
    yc.assignee_name,
    yc.year AS top_year,
    yc.apps_in_year
  FROM yearly_counts yc
  JOIN (
    SELECT
      assignee_name,
      MAX(apps_in_year) AS max_apps
    FROM yearly_counts
    GROUP BY assignee_name
  ) m ON yc.assignee_name = m.assignee_name AND yc.apps_in_year = m.max_apps
),
-- if multiple years tie, pick earliest year
top_year_dedup AS (
  SELECT
    assignee_name,
    MIN(top_year) AS top_year,
    MAX(apps_in_year) AS apps_in_top_year
  FROM top_year_per_assignee
  GROUP BY assignee_name
),
-- for each assignee and that top year, find country with most applications
country_counts AS (
  SELECT
    w.assignee_name,
    w.year,
    w.country_code,
    COUNT(DISTINCT w.application_number) AS apps_in_country_year
  FROM with_year w
  JOIN top_year_dedup t ON w.assignee_name = t.assignee_name AND w.year = t.top_year
  WHERE w.country_code IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY w.assignee_name, w.year, w.country_code
),
top_country AS (
  SELECT
    cc.assignee_name,
    cc.country_code,
    cc.apps_in_country_year
  FROM country_counts cc
  JOIN (
    SELECT assignee_name, MAX(apps_in_country_year) AS max_country_apps
    FROM country_counts
    GROUP BY assignee_name
  ) m ON cc.assignee_name = m.assignee_name AND cc.apps_in_country_year = m.max_country_apps
),
-- deduplicate if multiple countries tie: pick alphabetically first
top_country_dedup AS (
  SELECT
    assignee_name,
    MIN(country_code) AS country_code,
    MAX(apps_in_country_year) AS apps_in_country_year
  FROM top_country
  GROUP BY assignee_name
)
SELECT
  t.assignee_name AS assignee_name,
  t.total_applications AS total_applications,
  y.top_year AS year_with_most_applications,
  y.apps_in_top_year AS applications_in_that_year,
  c.country_code AS country_with_most_applications_in_that_year
FROM top3 t
LEFT JOIN top_year_dedup y ON t.assignee_name = y.assignee_name
LEFT JOIN top_country_dedup c ON t.assignee_name = c.assignee_name
ORDER BY t.total_applications DESC

WITH pubs AS (
  SELECT
    "publication_number" AS publication_number,
    "publication_date" AS publication_date,
    "country_code" AS country_code,
    "abstract_localized" AS abstract_localized
  FROM PATENTS.PATENTS.PUBLICATIONS
  WHERE "country_code" = 'US'
    AND "publication_date" IS NOT NULL
),
abstracts AS (
  SELECT
    publication_number,
    publication_date,
    -- extract all text values from abstract_localized variant (assumes object with language keys or string)
    CASE
      WHEN TYPEOF(abstract_localized) = 'STRING' THEN abstract_localized::STRING
      WHEN TYPEOF(abstract_localized) = 'OBJECT' THEN
        -- concatenate all language entries' text
        (SELECT LISTAGG(value::STRING, ' ') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY seq)
         FROM TABLE(FLATTEN(input => abstract_localized)) t(seq, key, value))
      WHEN TYPEOF(abstract_localized) = 'ARRAY' THEN
        (SELECT LISTAGG(value::STRING, ' ') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY seq)
         FROM TABLE(FLATTEN(input => abstract_localized)) t(seq, value))
      ELSE NULL
    END AS abstract_text
  FROM pubs
),
filtered AS (
  SELECT
    publication_number,
    -- convert publication_date (YYYYMMDD or YYYYMM) to DATE; handle numeric formats
    CASE
      WHEN LENGTH(TO_VARCHAR(publication_date)) >= 8 THEN TO_DATE(TO_VARCHAR(publication_date),'YYYYMMDD')
      WHEN LENGTH(TO_VARCHAR(publication_date)) = 6 THEN TO_DATE(TO_VARCHAR(publication_date)||'01','YYYYMMDD')
      WHEN LENGTH(TO_VARCHAR(publication_date)) = 4 THEN TO_DATE(TO_VARCHAR(publication_date)||'0101','YYYYMMDD')
      ELSE NULL
    END AS pub_date,
    abstract_text
  FROM abstracts
),
iot_pubs AS (
  SELECT
    publication_number,
    pub_date
  FROM filtered
  WHERE abstract_text ILIKE '%internet of things%'
    AND pub_date IS NOT NULL
    AND YEAR(pub_date) BETWEEN 2008 AND 2022
),
months AS (
  -- generate all months from Jan 2008 to Dec 2022
  SELECT DATEADD(month, seq4(), DATE_FROM_PARTS(2008,1,1)) AS month_start
  FROM TABLE(GENERATOR(ROWCOUNT => 12 * (2022 - 2008 + 1)))
),
counts AS (
  SELECT
    m.month_start,
    COUNT(i.publication_number) AS filings
  FROM months m
  LEFT JOIN iot_pubs i
    ON DATE_TRUNC('month', i.pub_date) = m.month_start
  GROUP BY m.month_start
)
SELECT
  TO_CHAR(month_start,'YYYY-MM') AS year_month,
  filings
FROM counts
ORDER BY month_start

WITH pubs AS (
  SELECT
    "publication_number" AS publication_number,
    "application_number" AS application_number,
    "publication_date" AS publication_date,
    "filing_date" AS filing_date,
    "kind_code" AS kind_code,
    "family_id" AS family_id,
    "publication_number" IS NOT NULL AS has_pub
  FROM PATENTS.PATENTS.PUBLICATIONS
),
-- select granted in 2010 utility patents: interpret kind_code starting with 'B' or grant_date present in year 2010.
granted2010 AS (
  SELECT
    publication_number,
    application_number,
    filing_date,
    publication_date
  FROM pubs
  WHERE
    -- grant in 2010: publication_date is epoch-like NUMBER; treat as YYYYMMDD or YYYY? assume YYYYMMDD; check between 20100101 and 20101231
    publication_date BETWEEN 20100101 AND 20101231
    -- utility patents: kind_code starting with 'B' (common convention)
    AND kind_code LIKE 'B%'
    AND filing_date IS NOT NULL
),
-- gather all potential citing publications by examining PUBLICATIONS.citation field which is VARIANT in base table.
-- We flatten citation arrays and capture citing application -> cited publication/application numbers and citation date if available.
cites AS (
  SELECT
    p."publication_number" AS citing_publication_number,
    p."application_number" AS citing_application_number,
    c.value:"publication_number"::string AS cited_publication_number,
    c.value:"application_number"::string AS cited_application_number,
    c.value:"date"::number AS citation_date,
    p."filing_date" AS citing_filing_date
  FROM PATENTS.PATENTS.PUBLICATIONS p,
  LATERAL FLATTEN(input => p."citation") c
),
-- normalize cited id: prefer cited_application_number, fallback to cited_publication_number
cites_norm AS (
  SELECT
    citing_publication_number,
    citing_application_number,
    COALESCE(NULLIF(cited_application_number,''), NULLIF(cited_publication_number,'')) AS cited_id,
    citation_date,
    citing_filing_date
  FROM cites
  WHERE COALESCE(NULLIF(cited_application_number,''), NULLIF(cited_publication_number,'')) IS NOT NULL
),
-- join granted2010 patents to citations where the cited_id matches the granted's application_number or publication_number,
-- and citation occurs within 10 years after the granted patent's filing_date (filing_date + 10 years).
-- Interpret filing_date as YYYYMMDD integer; add 1000000 for 10 years? Safer: convert to date via to_date(cast(filing_date as varchar), 'YYYYMMDD')
granted_citations AS (
  SELECT
    g.application_number AS target_application_number,
    g.publication_number AS target_publication_number,
    cn.citing_application_number AS citing_application_number,
    cn.citation_date AS citation_date,
    g.filing_date AS target_filing_date
  FROM granted2010 g
  JOIN cites_norm cn
    ON cn.cited_id IN (g.application_number, g.publication_number)
  WHERE
    g.filing_date IS NOT NULL
    -- compute dates: convert numeric YYYYMMDD to DATE; if filing_date length 8 assumed
    AND TRY_TO_DATE(TO_VARCHAR(g.filing_date), 'YYYYMMDD') IS NOT NULL
    AND (
      -- if citation_date present and parseable, use it; else fall back to citing_filing_date
      CASE
        WHEN TRY_TO_DATE(TO_VARCHAR(cn.citation_date), 'YYYYMMDD') IS NOT NULL
          THEN TRY_TO_DATE(TO_VARCHAR(cn.citation_date), 'YYYYMMDD')
        WHEN TRY_TO_DATE(TO_VARCHAR(cn.citing_filing_date), 'YYYYMMDD') IS NOT NULL
          THEN TRY_TO_DATE(TO_VARCHAR(cn.citing_filing_date), 'YYYYMMDD')
        ELSE NULL
      END
    ) IS NOT NULL
    AND (
      CASE
        WHEN TRY_TO_DATE(TO_VARCHAR(cn.citation_date), 'YYYYMMDD') IS NOT NULL
          THEN TRY_TO_DATE(TO_VARCHAR(cn.citation_date), 'YYYYMMDD')
        ELSE TRY_TO_DATE(TO_VARCHAR(cn.citing_filing_date), 'YYYYMMDD')
      END
    ) <= DATEADD(year, 10, TRY_TO_DATE(TO_VARCHAR(g.filing_date), 'YYYYMMDD'))
),
-- count distinct citing application numbers per target patent within window
counts AS (
  SELECT
    target_application_number,
    COUNT(DISTINCT citing_application_number) AS distinct_forward_citations
  FROM granted_citations
  WHERE citing_application_number IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY target_application_number
)
SELECT
  COUNT(*) AS patents_with_exactly_one_forward_citation
FROM counts
WHERE distinct_forward_citations = 1

WITH pubs AS (
  SELECT 
    "publication_number" AS publication_number,
    "grant_date" AS grant_date,
    "citation" AS citation
  FROM PATENTS.PATENTS.PUBLICATIONS
  WHERE "grant_date" BETWEEN 20100101 AND 20181231
),
flattened AS (
  SELECT

  FROM pubs,

),
filtered AS (

  FROM flattened

    cit:"category" = 'SEA'
)
SELECT

FROM filtered
GROUP BY publication_number
ORDER BY sea_backward_citation_count DESC, publication_number

WITH pubs AS (
  SELECT
    "publication_number" AS publication_number,
    "family_id"             AS family_id,
    "country_code"          AS country_code,
    "kind_code"             AS kind_code,
    "publication_date"      AS publication_date,
    "claims_localized"      AS claims_localized
  FROM PATENTS.PATENTS.PUBLICATIONS
  WHERE "country_code" = 'US'
    AND "kind_code" = 'B2'
    AND "publication_date" BETWEEN 20080000 AND 20181231
),
claims_extracted AS (
  SELECT
    publication_number,
    family_id,
    publication_date,
    -- claims_localized is VARIANT; extract text content. handle possible array/object structures by converting to string.
    IFF(claims_localized IS NULL, NULL, TO_VARIANT(claims_localized)) AS claims_variant
  FROM pubs
),
claims_text AS (
  SELECT
    publication_number,
    family_id,
    publication_date,
    -- try several approaches to get textual claim content:
    -- If claims_variant is an array of objects with 'text' fields, join them; otherwise stringify the variant.
    CASE
      WHEN TYPEOF(claims_variant) = 'ARRAY' THEN
        (SELECT LISTAGG(value:text::string, ' ') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY seq) FROM TABLE(FLATTEN(input => claims_variant)) t WHERE value IS NOT NULL)
      WHEN TYPEOF(claims_variant) = 'OBJECT' THEN
        -- try to extract any nested text fields by flattening object values
        (SELECT LISTAGG(v.value::string, ' ') FROM TABLE(FLATTEN(input => OBJECT_VALUES(claims_variant))) v WHERE v.value IS NOT NULL)
      ELSE
        TRY_TO_VARCHAR(claims_variant)
    END AS claims_text
  FROM claims_extracted
),
claims_flagged AS (
  SELECT
    publication_number,
    family_id,
    publication_date,
    claims_text,
    -- determine if claims_text does NOT contain the word 'claim' (case-insensitive, whole word)
    CASE
      WHEN claims_text IS NULL THEN FALSE
      WHEN REGEXP_LIKE(claims_text, '\\bclaim\\b', 'i') THEN FALSE
      ELSE TRUE
    END AS claims_without_word_claim
  FROM claims_text
)
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT publication_number) AS count_us_b2_no_claim_word_in_claims
FROM claims_flagged
WHERE claims_without_word_claim = TRUE

  FROM PATENTS.PATENTS.PUBLICATIONS

granted_cn AS (

    "id" AS id,
    "title" AS title,
    "abstract" AS abstract,
    "date" AS pub_date
  FROM PATENTSVIEW.PATENTSVIEW.PATENT
  WHERE "country" = 'US'
    AND TRY_TO_DATE("date",'YYYY-MM-DD') BETWEEN DATE '2014-01-01' AND DATE '2014-02-01'
),
cpc_filtered AS (
  -- keep patents that have CPC indicating chemistry/biology/medical per rules
  SELECT DISTINCT
    c."patent_id" AS patent_id
  FROM PATENTSVIEW.PATENTSVIEW.CPC_CURRENT c
  LEFT JOIN PATENTSVIEW.PATENTSVIEW.CPC_SUBSECTION cs ON c."subsection_id" = cs."id"
  WHERE 1=1
    -- subsection id between C5 and C13 (string compare on leading letter+number)
    AND (
      (c."subsection_id" IS NOT NULL AND TRY_TO_NUMBER(REGEXP_REPLACE(c."subsection_id",'[^0-9]','')) IS NOT NULL
        AND LEFT(c."subsection_id",1) = 'C'
        AND TRY_TO_NUMBER(SPLIT_PART(c."subsection_id",'C',2)) BETWEEN 5 AND 13)
      OR
      -- or group id in provided set
      (c."group_id" IN ('A01G','A01H','A61K','A61P','A61Q','B01F','B01J','B81B','B82B','B82Y','G01N','G16H'))
    )
),
patents AS (
  SELECT p.id, p.title, p.abstract, TRY_TO_DATE(p.pub_date,'YYYY-MM-DD') AS pub_date
  FROM patents_base p
  JOIN cpc_filtered cf ON p.id = cf.patent_id
),
-- backward citations: count citations made by the patent (USPATENTCITATION) where cited patent date < filing/publication date
-- we treat patent's filing date as pub_date here because filing not available in PATENT table; using pub_date to approximate filing date per instructions
back_counts AS (
  SELECT
    uc."patent_id" AS patent_id,
    COUNT(*) AS backward_citations
  FROM PATENTSVIEW.PATENTSVIEW.USPATENTCITATION uc
  JOIN patents pt ON uc."patent_id" = pt.id
  LEFT JOIN PATENTSVIEW.PATENTSVIEW.PATENT cited ON uc."citation_id" = cited."id"
  WHERE
    -- consider only citations to patents (citation_id matches PATENT.id)
    uc."citation_id" IS NOT NULL
    -- count if the cited patent's date is before the focal patent's publication date
    AND (TRY_TO_DATE(cited."date",'YYYY-MM-DD') < pt.pub_date OR cited."date" IS NULL AND FALSE)
  GROUP BY uc."patent_id"
),
-- forward citations: count patents that cite the focal patent within 5 years after focal pub_date
forward_candidates AS (
  -- using USPATENTCITATION where citation_id = focal patent id; the citing patent is uc."patent_id"
  SELECT
    cited_id."id" AS focal_id,
    citing_uc."patent_id" AS citing_patent_id,
    TRY_TO_DATE(citing_pat."date",'YYYY-MM-DD') AS citing_pub_date,
    cited_pt.pub_date AS focal_pub_date
  FROM PATENTSVIEW.PATENTSVIEW.USPATENTCITATION citing_uc
  JOIN patents cited_pt ON citing_uc."citation_id" = cited_pt.id
  JOIN PATENTSVIEW.PATENTSVIEW.PATENT cited_id ON citing_uc."citation_id" = cited_id."id"
  LEFT JOIN PATENTSVIEW.PATENTSVIEW.PATENT citing_pat ON citing_uc."patent_id" = citing_pat."id"
  WHERE citing_uc."citation_id" IS NOT NULL
),
forward_counts AS (
  SELECT
    focal_id AS patent_id,
    COUNT(DISTINCT citing_patent_id) AS forward_citations_5yr
  FROM forward_candidates
  WHERE citing_pub_date IS NOT NULL
    AND focal_pub_date IS NOT NULL
    AND citing_pub_date >= focal_pub_date
    AND citing_pub_date < DATEADD(year,5,focal_pub_date)
  GROUP BY focal_id
)
SELECT
  p.id AS patent_id,
  p.title,
  p.abstract,
  TO_VARCHAR(p.pub_date,'YYYY-MM-DD') AS publication_date,
  COALESCE(b.backward_citations,0) AS backward_citations,
  COALESCE(f.forward_citations_5yr,0) AS forward_citations_5yr
FROM patents p
LEFT JOIN back_counts b ON p.id = b.patent_id
LEFT JOIN forward_counts f ON p.id = f.patent_id
ORDER BY p.pub_date, p.id

  SELECT

    t18.median_income AS median_income_2018,

WITH

FROM features_with_wikidata

tx_gas_fees AS (
  SELECT
    t."block_number" AS block_number,

  FROM ETHEREUM_BLOCKCHAIN.ETHEREUM_BLOCKCHAIN.TRANSACTIONS t

miner_rewards AS (

    UNION

    SELECT "miner" AS addr FROM ETHEREUM_BLOCKCHAIN.ETHEREUM_BLOCKCHAIN.BLOCKS WHERE COALESCE("miner",'') <> ''

    f.first_purchase_date,
    f.first_purchase_month,
    o.order_date,
    -- months_between gives fractional months; use month difference by year/month calculation
    (DATE_PART('year', o.order_date) - DATE_PART('year', f.first_purchase_date)) * 12
      + (DATE_PART('month', o.order_date) - DATE_PART('month', f.first_purchase_date)) AS month_offset
  FROM first_purchase f
  JOIN orders o
    ON f.user_id = o.user_id
),
user_bucket_flags AS (
  -- For each user, determine if they had any purchase in month_offset 0,1,2,3 (first..fourth month)
  SELECT
    user_id,
    first_purchase_month,
    MAX(CASE WHEN month_offset = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS month_1_flag,
    MAX(CASE WHEN month_offset = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS month_2_flag,
    MAX(CASE WHEN month_offset = 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS month_3_flag,
    MAX(CASE WHEN month_offset = 3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS month_4_flag
  FROM user_month_purchases
  WHERE month_offset BETWEEN 0 AND 3
  GROUP BY user_id, first_purchase_month
),
monthly_totals AS (
  SELECT
    first_purchase_month,
    COUNT(*) AS users_in_month
  FROM user_bucket_flags
  GROUP BY first_purchase_month
)
SELECT
  t.first_purchase_month AS first_purchase_month,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(ubf.month_1_flag) / NULLIF(t.users_in_month,0),2) AS pct_first_month,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(ubf.month_2_flag) / NULLIF(t.users_in_month,0),2) AS pct_second_month,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(ubf.month_3_flag) / NULLIF(t.users_in_month,0),2) AS pct_third_month,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(ubf.month_4_flag) / NULLIF(t.users_in_month,0),2) AS pct_fourth_month,
  t.users_in_month
FROM monthly_totals t
JOIN user_bucket_flags ubf
  ON t.first_purchase_month = ubf.first_purchase_month
GROUP BY t.first_purchase_month, t.users_in_month
ORDER BY t.first_purchase_month

WITH
-- base order items joined to orders and products to get only completed orders and category + month
order_items_base AS (
  SELECT
    "oi"."id" AS oi_id,
    "oi"."order_id" AS order_id,
    "oi"."sale_price" AS sale_price,
    "p"."category" AS category,
    TO_CHAR(TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ("o"."delivered_at"), 'YYYY-MM') AS year_month
  FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDER_ITEMS "oi"
  JOIN THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDERS "o"
    ON "oi"."order_id" = "o"."order_id"
  JOIN THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.PRODUCTS "p"
    ON "oi"."product_id" = "p"."id"
  WHERE "o"."status" = 'completed'
    AND "o"."delivered_at" IS NOT NULL
    AND "p"."category" IS NOT NULL
),
-- unique orders per category-month
orders_per_month AS (
  SELECT
    category,
    year_month,
    COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS orders_count,
    SUM(sale_price) AS revenue
  FROM order_items_base
  GROUP BY category, year_month
),
-- generate previous month per category by ordering months; compute pct change month-over-month
orders_with_lag AS (
  SELECT
    category,
    year_month,
    orders_count,
    revenue,
    LAG(orders_count) OVER (PARTITION BY category ORDER BY year_month) AS prev_orders_count,
    LAG(revenue)      OVER (PARTITION BY category ORDER BY year_month) AS prev_revenue
  FROM orders_per_month
),
-- compute percentage changes, filtering out months where prev is null or zero (to avoid infinite pct change)
pct_changes AS (
  SELECT
    category,
    year_month,
    CASE
      WHEN prev_orders_count IS NULL OR prev_orders_count = 0 THEN NULL
      ELSE (orders_count::FLOAT - prev_orders_count::FLOAT) / prev_orders_count::FLOAT
    END AS orders_pct_change,
    CASE
      WHEN prev_revenue IS NULL OR prev_revenue = 0 THEN NULL
      ELSE (revenue::FLOAT - prev_revenue::FLOAT) / prev_revenue::FLOAT
    END AS revenue_pct_change
  FROM orders_with_lag
),
-- average the monthly pct changes per category (ignore NULLs)
avg_pct_by_category AS (
  SELECT
    category,
    AVG(orders_pct_change) AS avg_monthly_orders_pct_change,
    AVG(revenue_pct_change) AS avg_monthly_revenue_pct_change
  FROM pct_changes
  GROUP BY category
),
-- pick the category with highest average monthly orders pct change
top_category AS (
  SELECT
    category,
    avg_monthly_orders_pct_change,
    avg_monthly_revenue_pct_change
  FROM avg_pct_by_category
  QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY avg_monthly_orders_pct_change DESC NULLS LAST) = 1
)
-- final output: the category and its two averaged metrics
SELECT
  tc.category AS top_category,
  tc.avg_monthly_orders_pct_change AS average_monthly_order_growth_rate,
  tc.avg_monthly_revenue_pct_change AS average_monthly_revenue_growth_rate
FROM top_category tc

WITH users_filtered AS (

  WHERE "created_at" BETWEEN 1546300800 AND 1651276799
    AND "age" IS NOT NULL

),
gender_stats AS (

    MIN(age) AS min_age,
    MAX(age) AS max_age
  FROM users_filtered
  GROUP BY gender
),
young_counts AS (
  SELECT
    g.gender,
    g.min_age AS age,
    COUNT(u.id) AS user_count,
    'youngest' AS age_type
  FROM gender_stats g
  JOIN users_filtered u
    ON u.gender = g.gender
   AND u.age = g.min_age
  GROUP BY g.gender, g.min_age
),
old_counts AS (
  SELECT
    g.gender,
    g.max_age AS age,
    COUNT(u.id) AS user_count,
    'oldest' AS age_type
  FROM gender_stats g
  JOIN users_filtered u

   AND u.age = g.max_age
  GROUP BY g.gender, g.max_age
)
SELECT

FROM (

  SELECT * FROM old_counts
)

WITH order_items AS (

oi_with_month AS (

  FROM order_items oi

),
-- The WHERE above is clumsy; replace with explicit check for before 2024-01-01
oi_with_month_fixed AS (

monthly_product_agg AS (

WITH order_items_cte AS (
  SELECT
    "order_id" AS order_id,
    "product_id" AS product_id,
    "sale_price" AS sale_price,
    "created_at" AS created_at
  FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDER_ITEMS
),
products_cte AS (
  SELECT
    "id" AS product_id,
    "category" AS category,
    "cost" AS cost
  FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.PRODUCTS
),
orders_cte AS (
  SELECT
    "order_id" AS order_id,
    "created_at" AS order_created_at
  FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDERS
),
-- Join order items to products and orders, compute month (YYYY-MM) and revenue/profit
joined AS (
  SELECT
    TO_CHAR(TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ(o.order_created_at/1000), 'YYYY-MM') AS month,
    p.category AS category,
    oi.order_id AS order_id,
    COALESCE(oi.sale_price,0) AS revenue,
    COALESCE(oi.sale_price,0) - COALESCE(p.cost,0) AS profit
  FROM order_items_cte oi
  LEFT JOIN products_cte p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
  LEFT JOIN orders_cte o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
  WHERE TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ(o.order_created_at/1000) >= TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ(DATE_PART(epoch, '2019-06-01'::timestamp)) -- keep June+ but ensure non-null
    OR TO_CHAR(TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ(o.order_created_at/1000), 'YYYY-MM') IS NOT NULL
),
-- Aggregate per month and category
monthly AS (
  SELECT
    month,
    category,
    COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS total_orders,
    SUM(revenue) AS total_revenue,
    SUM(profit) AS total_profit
  FROM joined
  WHERE month BETWEEN '2019-06' AND '2019-12'
  GROUP BY month, category
),
-- Extract June baseline per category
june_baseline AS (
  SELECT
    category,
    total_orders AS june_orders,
    total_revenue AS june_revenue,
    total_profit AS june_profit
  FROM monthly
  WHERE month = '2019-06'
),
-- Prepare final rows for months July-Dec, join baseline for growth calc
final_prep AS (
  SELECT
    m.month,
    m.category,
    m.total_orders,
    m.total_revenue,
    m.total_profit,
    jb.june_orders,
    jb.june_revenue,
    jb.june_profit
  FROM monthly m
  LEFT JOIN june_baseline jb ON m.category = jb.category
  WHERE m.month BETWEEN '2019-07' AND '2019-12'
)
SELECT
  month,
  category,
  total_orders,
  total_revenue,
  total_profit,
  -- Growth rates compared to June baseline. If baseline is zero or NULL, show NULL to avoid division by zero.
  CASE WHEN june_orders IS NULL OR june_orders = 0 THEN NULL ELSE (total_orders - june_orders) / june_orders END AS orders_mom_growth_vs_june,
  CASE WHEN june_revenue IS NULL OR june_revenue = 0 THEN NULL ELSE (total_revenue - june_revenue) / june_revenue END AS revenue_mom_growth_vs_june,
  CASE WHEN june_profit IS NULL OR june_profit = 0 THEN NULL ELSE (total_profit - june_profit) / june_profit END AS profit_mom_growth_vs_june
FROM final_prep
ORDER BY month ASC, category ASC

),
orders AS (

products AS (

),
items_joined AS (

monthly_aggregates AS (

WITH users_2019 AS (
  SELECT "id" AS id,
         "email" AS email,
         "created_at" AS created_at
  FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.USERS
  WHERE "created_at" BETWEEN 1546300800 AND 1577836799
),
orders_2019 AS (
  SELECT "order_id" AS order_id,
         "user_id" AS user_id,
         "created_at" AS created_at,
         "num_of_item" AS num_of_item
  FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDERS
  WHERE "created_at" BETWEEN 1546300800 AND 1577836799
),
order_items_2019 AS (
  SELECT "order_id" AS order_id,
         "user_id" AS user_id,
         "sale_price" AS sale_price
  FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDER_ITEMS oi
  WHERE EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDERS o
    WHERE o."order_id" = oi."order_id"
      AND o."created_at" BETWEEN 1546300800 AND 1577836799
  )
),
-- compute total order value per order by summing (num_of_item * sale_price) across items;
-- but num_of_item is at order level; assume sale_price per order_item represents price per item line.
order_value_per_order AS (
  SELECT o.order_id,
         o.user_id,
         o.num_of_item,
         COALESCE(SUM(oi.sale_price * o.num_of_item), 0) AS order_value
  FROM orders_2019 o
  LEFT JOIN order_items_2019 oi
    ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
  GROUP BY o.order_id, o.user_id, o.num_of_item
),
user_order_aggregates AS (
  SELECT u.id AS user_id,
         u.email AS email,
         COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders,
         SUM(o.order_value) AS total_value
  FROM users_2019 u
  JOIN order_value_per_order o
    ON u.id = o.user_id
  GROUP BY u.id, u.email
),
user_avg_order_value AS (
  SELECT user_id,
         email,
         total_value / NULLIF(total_orders,0) AS avg_order_value
  FROM user_order_aggregates
)
SELECT email
FROM user_avg_order_value
ORDER BY avg_order_value DESC
LIMIT 10

WITH order_items AS (
  SELECT
    "id" AS id,
    "order_id" AS order_id,
    "user_id" AS user_id,
    "product_id" AS product_id,
    "inventory_item_id" AS inventory_item_id,
    "status" AS status,
    "created_at" AS created_at,
    "shipped_at" AS shipped_at,
    "delivered_at" AS delivered_at,
    "returned_at" AS returned_at,
    "sale_price" AS sale_price
  FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDER_ITEMS
),
orders AS (
  SELECT
    "order_id" AS order_id,
    "user_id" AS user_id,
    "status" AS status,
    "gender" AS gender,
    "created_at" AS created_at,
    "returned_at" AS returned_at,
    "shipped_at" AS shipped_at,
    "delivered_at" AS delivered_at,
    "num_of_item" AS num_of_item
  FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDERS
),
products AS (
  SELECT
    "id" AS id,
    "cost" AS cost,
    "category" AS category,
    "name" AS name,
    "brand" AS brand,
    "retail_price" AS retail_price,
    "department" AS department,
    "sku" AS sku,
    "distribution_center_id" AS distribution_center_id
  FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.PRODUCTS
),
-- join order_items to orders to get order created_at (assume order created_at is the sale time)
sales AS (
  SELECT
    oi.product_id AS product_id,
    o.created_at AS order_created_at
  FROM order_items oi
  JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
  WHERE o.created_at IS NOT NULL
),
-- filter to 2020 and extract month
sales_2020 AS (
  SELECT
    product_id,
    TO_DATE(TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ(order_created_at)) AS order_date,
    DATE_TRUNC('month', TO_DATE(TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ(order_created_at))) AS month_start
  FROM sales
  WHERE DATE_PART('year', TO_DATE(TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ(order_created_at))) = 2020
),
-- compute profit per product from products table (retail_price - cost)
product_profit AS (
  SELECT
    id AS product_id,
    name AS product_name,
    retail_price,
    cost,
    (retail_price - cost) AS profit
  FROM products
),
-- for each month and product that had at least one sale, get profit
month_product_profit AS (
  SELECT
    s.month_start AS month_start,
    pp.product_id AS product_id,
    pp.product_name AS product_name,
    pp.profit AS profit
  FROM (
    SELECT DISTINCT month_start, product_id
    FROM sales_2020
  ) s
  JOIN product_profit pp ON s.product_id = pp.product_id
  WHERE pp.profit IS NOT NULL
),
-- for each month find the minimum profit
month_min_profit AS (
  SELECT
    month_start,
    MIN(profit) AS min_profit
  FROM month_product_profit
  GROUP BY month_start
)
-- final: products per month whose profit equals the month's minimum, order chronologically
SELECT
  TO_CHAR(mmp.month_start, 'YYYY-MM') AS month,
  mpp.product_name AS product_name,
  mpp.profit AS profit
FROM month_min_profit mmp
JOIN month_product_profit mpp
  ON mmp.month_start = mpp.month_start
 AND mmp.min_profit = mpp.profit
ORDER BY mmp.month_start ASC, mpp.product_name ASC

WITH events AS (

  FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.EVENTS
),
session_bounds AS (
  SELECT
    session_id,

    MAX(created_at) AS session_end_ts
  FROM events
  GROUP BY session_id, browser
),
session_durations AS (

    session_id,

  FROM session_bounds
),
browser_stats AS (

FROM browser_stats

WITH first_purchases AS (
  SELECT
    "user_id" AS user_id,
    MIN("created_at") AS first_purchase_ts
  FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDERS
  GROUP BY "user_id"
),
jan2020_cohort AS (
  SELECT
    user_id,

    DATE_TRUNC('month', TO_TIMESTAMP(first_purchase_ts)) AS first_purchase_month
  FROM first_purchases
  WHERE DATE_TRUNC('month', TO_TIMESTAMP(first_purchase_ts)) = DATE '2020-01-01'
),
user_returns AS (
  SELECT
    o."user_id" AS user_id,
    -- consider returned_at on orders; convert to date
    CASE WHEN o."returned_at" IS NOT NULL THEN DATE(TO_TIMESTAMP(o."returned_at")) END AS returned_date
  FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDERS o
  WHERE o."returned_at" IS NOT NULL
),
cohort_returns_by_month AS (
  SELECT
    c.user_id AS user_id,
    DATE_TRUNC('month', ur.returned_date) AS return_month
  FROM jan2020_cohort c
  LEFT JOIN user_returns ur
    ON c.user_id = ur.user_id
  WHERE ur.returned_date IS NOT NULL
    AND ur.returned_date >= DATE '2020-01-01'
    AND ur.returned_date < DATE '2021-01-01'
),
-- For each cohort user, mark months in 2020 they returned (unique)
user_month_flags AS (
  SELECT
    user_id,
    return_month
  FROM cohort_returns_by_month
  GROUP BY user_id, return_month
),
months_2020 AS (
  SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', DATEADD(month, seq4(), DATE '2020-01-01')) AS month_start

),
cohort_size AS (

),
monthly_return_rates AS (

  FROM months_2020 m

WITH
orders_cte AS (

    "order_id" AS order_id,

    "created_at" AS created_at
  FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDERS

),
users_cte AS (

    "id" AS id,

inventory_cte AS (

  FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.INVENTORY_ITEMS

order_items_cte AS (

products_cte AS (

    "department" AS department,

  FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.PRODUCTS

-- Join orders to users (users registered in 2021 already filtered), ensure order's user is such a user
orders_users AS (
  SELECT
    o.order_id AS order_id,

    o.created_at AS order_created_at

-- Join order items to inventory items created in 2021
order_items_inventory AS (

  JOIN inventory_cte inv

-- Combine everything and attach product details
combined AS (

  JOIN order_items_inventory oii

  WHERE ou.order_created_at BETWEEN 1609459200 AND 1640995199

  department,

WITH order_items AS (
  SELECT
    "id" AS id,
    "order_id" AS order_id,
    "product_id" AS product_id,
    "inventory_item_id" AS inventory_item_id,
    "status" AS status,
    "created_at" AS created_at,
    "shipped_at" AS shipped_at,
    "delivered_at" AS delivered_at,
    "returned_at" AS returned_at,
    "sale_price" AS sale_price
  FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDER_ITEMS
),
orders AS (
  SELECT
    "order_id" AS order_id,
    "status" AS status,
    "created_at" AS created_at
  FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDERS
),
inventory AS (
  SELECT
    "id" AS id,
    "product_id" AS product_id,
    "cost" AS cost,
    "sold_at" AS sold_at
  FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.INVENTORY_ITEMS
),
products AS (
  SELECT
    "id" AS id,
    "name" AS name
  FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.PRODUCTS
),
-- join order items to orders and inventory to get sale_price and cost and filter out canceled/returned orders/order_items
valid_sales AS (
  SELECT
    oi.product_id AS product_id,
    oi.sale_price AS sale_price,
    inv.cost AS cost,
    -- determine sale month from order item's created_at (use delivered_at if available else created_at)
    COALESCE(oi.delivered_at, oi.shipped_at, oi.created_at) AS ts
  FROM order_items oi
  JOIN orders o
    ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
  LEFT JOIN inventory inv
    ON oi.inventory_item_id = inv.id
  WHERE
    -- exclude orders with cancelled/returned statuses
    LOWER(o.status) NOT IN ('canceled','cancelled','returned')
    -- exclude order_items that themselves are returned/cancelled
    AND LOWER(oi.status) NOT IN ('canceled','cancelled','returned')
    -- ensure timestamp present
    AND COALESCE(oi.delivered_at, oi.shipped_at, oi.created_at) IS NOT NULL
    -- ensure sale within range Jan 2019 - Aug 2022 (use Unix epoch ms or seconds? assuming numeric epoch seconds)
    AND DATE_TRUNC('month', TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ(COALESCE(oi.delivered_at, oi.shipped_at, oi.created_at))) 
        BETWEEN TO_DATE('2019-01-01') AND TO_DATE('2022-08-31')
),
monthly_profit AS (
  SELECT
    DATE_TRUNC('month', TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ(ts))::DATE AS month,
    product_id,
    SUM( COALESCE(sale_price,0) ) AS total_sales,
    SUM( COALESCE(cost,0) ) AS total_cost,
    SUM( COALESCE(sale_price,0) ) - SUM( COALESCE(cost,0) ) AS profit
  FROM valid_sales
  GROUP BY 1,2
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT
    mp.month,
    mp.product_id,
    p.name AS product_name,
    mp.profit,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY mp.month ORDER BY mp.profit DESC) AS rn
  FROM monthly_profit mp
  LEFT JOIN products p
    ON mp.product_id = p.id
)
SELECT
  TO_CHAR(month, 'YYYY-MM') AS month,
  product_id,
  product_name,
  profit
FROM ranked
WHERE rn <= 3
ORDER BY month, profit DESC

WITH orders_cte AS (

    "order_id" AS order_id,

  FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDERS
  WHERE "created_at" BETWEEN 1661990400 AND 1701369599 -- Aug 1 2022 00:00:00 UTC to Nov 30 2023 23:59:59 UTC
    AND "status" = 'completed'
),
users_cte AS (

products_cte AS (

with_lag AS (

WITH variants AS (
  SELECT
    "reference_name" AS reference_name
  FROM GENOMICS_CANNABIS.GENOMICS_CANNABIS.MNPR01_201703
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    "reference_name" AS reference_name
  FROM GENOMICS_CANNABIS.GENOMICS_CANNABIS.MNPR01_TRANSCRIPTOME_201703
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    "reference_name" AS reference_name
  FROM GENOMICS_CANNABIS.GENOMICS_CANNABIS.CS3K_VCF_CS10_DV090
),
reference_lengths AS (
  SELECT
    "name" AS name,
    "length" AS length
  FROM GENOMICS_CANNABIS.GENOMICS_CANNABIS.MNPR01_REFERENCE_201703
),
counts AS (
  SELECT
    v.reference_name AS reference_name,
    COUNT(*) AS variant_count
  FROM variants v
  GROUP BY v.reference_name
),
density AS (
  SELECT
    c.reference_name AS reference_name,
    c.variant_count AS variant_count,
    r.length AS reference_length,
    CASE WHEN r.length > 0 THEN c.variant_count::FLOAT / r.length ELSE NULL END AS variants_per_base
  FROM counts c
  LEFT JOIN reference_lengths r
    ON c.reference_name = r.name
)
SELECT
  reference_name,
  variant_count,
  reference_length,
  variants_per_base
FROM density
ORDER BY variants_per_base DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 1

WITH refs AS (
  SELECT "name" AS name, "length" AS length
  FROM GENOMICS_CANNABIS.GENOMICS_CANNABIS.MNPR01_REFERENCE_201703
),
longest_ref AS (
  SELECT name, length
  FROM refs
  ORDER BY length DESC
  LIMIT 1
),
-- gather variant calls across the variant tables that reference the reference sequence
variants AS (
  SELECT
    "reference_name" AS reference_name,
    "start" AS start_pos,
    "end" AS end_pos,
    "call" AS call
  FROM GENOMICS_CANNABIS.GENOMICS_CANNABIS.MNPR01_TRANSCRIPTOME_201703
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    "reference_name" AS reference_name,
    "start" AS start_pos,
    "end" AS end_pos,
    "call" AS call
  FROM GENOMICS_CANNABIS.GENOMICS_CANNABIS.MNPR01_201703
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    "reference_name" AS reference_name,
    "start_position" AS start_pos,
    "end_position" AS end_pos,
    "call" AS call
  FROM GENOMICS_CANNABIS.GENOMICS_CANNABIS.CS3K_VCF_CS10_DV090
),
-- extract genotypes from call objects; VCF "call" can be VARIANT (array/object). We handle both object and array forms.
calls_exploded AS (
  SELECT
    v.reference_name,
    v.start_pos,
    v.end_pos,
    c.value:"GT"::STRING AS gt_str
  FROM variants v,
  LATERAL FLATTEN(input => v.call) c
),
-- normalize genotype value to numeric allele counts: consider formats like "0/1", "1|1", "1", or numeric string
calls_parsed AS (
  SELECT
    reference_name,
    start_pos,
    end_pos,
    gt_str,
    TRY_TO_NUMBER(REGEXP_REPLACE(gt_str, '[^0-9|/]', '')) AS gt_num_guess,
    -- compute whether any allele > 0
    CASE
      WHEN gt_str IS NULL THEN FALSE
      WHEN gt_str LIKE '%/%' OR gt_str LIKE '%|%' THEN
        -- split alleles and check max > 0
        (GREATEST(
           TRY_TO_NUMBER(SPLIT_PART(gt_str, '/', 1)),
           TRY_TO_NUMBER(SPLIT_PART(gt_str, '/', 2)),
           TRY_TO_NUMBER(SPLIT_PART(gt_str, '|', 1)),
           TRY_TO_NUMBER(SPLIT_PART(gt_str, '|', 2))
         ) > 0)
      ELSE
        -- single allele string or numeric
        (TRY_TO_NUMBER(gt_str) > 0)
    END AS has_variant
  FROM calls_exploded
),
-- per variant record (by reference and position) determine if any call indicates variant (has_variant true)
variant_positions AS (
  SELECT
    reference_name,
    start_pos,
    end_pos,
    MAX(CASE WHEN has_variant THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS is_variant
  FROM calls_parsed
  GROUP BY reference_name, start_pos, end_pos
),
-- count variant positions for the longest reference
variant_count AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS variant_positions
  FROM variant_positions vp
  JOIN longest_ref lr ON vp.reference_name = lr.name
  WHERE vp.is_variant = 1
)
SELECT
  lr.name AS reference_name,
  lr.length AS reference_length,
  vc.variant_positions,
  CASE WHEN lr.length > 0 THEN vc.variant_positions::FLOAT / lr.length ELSE NULL END AS variants_per_base
FROM longest_ref lr
CROSS JOIN variant_count vc

WITH all_tx AS (
  SELECT "block_timestamp" AS block_timestamp
  FROM GOOG_BLOCKCHAIN.GOOG_BLOCKCHAIN_CRONOS_MAINNET_US.TRANSACTIONS
  WHERE DATE_PART(year, "block_timestamp") = 2023
  UNION ALL
  SELECT "block_timestamp" AS block_timestamp
  FROM GOOG_BLOCKCHAIN.GOOG_BLOCKCHAIN_POLYGON_MAINNET_US.TRANSACTIONS
  WHERE DATE_PART(year, "block_timestamp") = 2023
),
tx_by_month AS (
  SELECT
    DATE_PART(year, block_timestamp) AS year,
    DATE_PART(month, block_timestamp) AS month,
    COUNT(*) AS tx_count,
    MIN(DATE_TRUNC('month', block_timestamp)) AS month_start
  FROM all_tx
  GROUP BY DATE_PART(year, block_timestamp), DATE_PART(month, block_timestamp)
)
SELECT
  tx_count,
  tx_count / (DATE_PART(epoch_second, DATEADD(month, 1, month_start)) - DATE_PART(epoch_second, month_start)) AS tx_per_second,
  year,
  month
FROM tx_by_month
ORDER BY tx_count DESC

WITH decoded AS (
  SELECT
    "transaction_hash" AS transaction_hash,
    "block_number" AS block_number,
    "address" AS log_address,
    "topics" AS topics,
    "data" AS data
  FROM GOOG_BLOCKCHAIN.GOOG_BLOCKCHAIN_ARBITRUM_ONE_US.LOGS
  WHERE "block_number" = 29815485
),
-- find logs whose first topic = DepositFinalized keccak hash
deposit_logs AS (
  SELECT
    transaction_hash,
    block_number,
    log_address,
    topics,
    data,
    -- topics is VARIANT array; topic0 at index 0
    topics[0]::string AS topic0
  FROM decoded
  WHERE topics IS NOT NULL
    AND topics[0]::string = '0x3303facd24627943a92e9dc87cfbb34b15c49b726eec3ad3487c16be9ab8efe8'
),
-- parse event parameters for Optimism DepositFinalized:
-- DepositFinalized(address _l1Token, address _l2Token, address _from, address _to, uint256 _amount)
-- In many ABIs, indexed fields appear in topics; assume topics layout:
-- topics[1] = indexed l1Token, topics[2] = indexed l2Token, topics[3] = indexed from OR to depending on bridge
-- To be robust, parse addresses from topics[1..3] and amount from data (last 32 bytes)
parsed AS (
  SELECT
    transaction_hash,
    block_number,
    log_address,
    -- extract topic 1..3 as strings
    topics[1]::string AS topic1,
    topics[2]::string AS topic2,
    topics[3]::string AS topic3,
    data::string AS data_str
  FROM deposit_logs
),
-- helper to strip '0x' and leading zeroes from hex addresses (keep at least one zero)
strip_addr AS (
  SELECT
    transaction_hash,
    block_number,
    log_address,
    -- remove 0x prefix then take rightmost 40 hex chars in case topics are 32-byte padded
    LOWER(REGEXP_REPLACE(SUBSTR(topic1, 3 + GREATEST(0, LENGTH(topic1) - 2 - 40)), '^0+', '')) AS l1_token,
    LOWER(REGEXP_REPLACE(SUBSTR(topic2, 3 + GREATEST(0, LENGTH(topic2) - 2 - 40)), '^0+', '')) AS l2_token,
    LOWER(REGEXP_REPLACE(SUBSTR(topic3, 3 + GREATEST(0, LENGTH(topic3) - 2 - 40)), '^0+', '')) AS sender_or_receiver_topic,
    data_str
  FROM parsed
),
-- amount is in data field; data may be 0x + 32-byte hex representing amount (or multiple fields). We take last 64 hex chars as uint256
amounts AS (
  SELECT
    transaction_hash,
    block_number,
    log_address,
    l1_token,
    l2_token,
    sender_or_receiver_topic,
    data_str,
    -- take last 64 hex chars of data (after 0x)
    CASE
      WHEN data_str IS NULL THEN NULL
      ELSE
        -- remove 0x then take rightmost 64 chars, then convert hex to decimal
        TO_NUMBER('0x' || RIGHT(REGEXP_REPLACE(data_str, '^0x', ''), 64))
    END AS amount_decimal
  FROM strip_addr
),
-- derive sender and receiver: Optimism DepositFinalized typically has _from and _to as non-indexed? If topics[3] is the depositor (from) we use that as sender; receiver may be encoded in data if present.
-- We'll assume topics[3] holds the 'from' address and the 'to' is encoded in data preceding amount (common layout: data = abi.encode(to, amount) -> first 32 bytes = to)
final AS (
  SELECT
    transaction_hash,
    block_number,
    l1_token,
    l2_token,
    -- sender: from topics[3] -> strip 0x and left-pad then remove leading zeroes
    CASE
      WHEN sender_or_receiver_topic IS NULL THEN NULL
      ELSE LOWER(REGEXP_REPLACE(SUBSTR(sender_or_receiver_topic, 3 + GREATEST(0, LENGTH(sender_or_receiver_topic) - 2 - 40)), '^0+', ''))
    END AS sender,
    -- extract 'to' from data: first 32 bytes (after 0x) -> rightmost 40 chars of that 64-hex chunk
    CASE
      WHEN data_str IS NULL THEN NULL
      ELSE LOWER(REGEXP_REPLACE(SUBSTR(RIGHT(LPAD(REGEXP_REPLACE(data_str, '^0x', ''), 128, '0'), 128), 1, 64), '^0+', ''))
    END AS to_prefixed,
    amount_decimal
  FROM amounts
),
final2 AS (
  SELECT
    transaction_hash,
    block_number,
    l1_token,
    l2_token,
    sender,
    -- to_prefixed may be 64 hex chars (address right-padded in 32 bytes); take rightmost 40 chars and strip leading zeroes
    CASE
      WHEN to_prefixed IS NULL THEN NULL
      ELSE LOWER(REGEXP_REPLACE(RIGHT(to_prefixed, 40), '^0+', ''))
    END AS receiver,
    amount_decimal
  FROM final
)
SELECT
  transaction_hash,
  -- full Etherscan tx URL for Optimism (optimistic etherscan mainnet): https://optimistic.etherscan.io/tx/{txhash}
  'https://optimistic.etherscan.io/tx/' || transaction_hash AS etherscan_url,
  -- remove any leading zeros already stripped; ensure empty string if null
  COALESCE(NULLIF(l1_token, ''), NULL) AS l1_token,
  COALESCE(NULLIF(l2_token, ''), NULL) AS l2_token,
  COALESCE(NULLIF(sender, ''), NULL) AS sender,
  COALESCE(NULLIF(receiver, ''), NULL) AS receiver,
  amount_decimal
FROM final2
ORDER BY transaction_hash

    "reputation" AS reputation,
    "creation_date" AS creation_date,
    "creation_date"::timestamp_ntz(0) AS creation_ts
  FROM STACKOVERFLOW.STACKOVERFLOW.USERS
  WHERE "creation_date" IS NOT NULL

users_cutoff AS (
  SELECT
    id,
    reputation,
    creation_date,

  WHERE creation_ts <= TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ('2021-10-01 00:00:00')

  SELECT

    -- compute complete years between creation date and cutoff date 2021-10-01
    FLOOR(DATEDIFF(year, creation_ts, TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ('2021-10-01 00:00:00'))

  FROM users_cutoff

  SELECT

  GROUP BY "user_id"

)

  COUNT(*) AS users_in_bin,
  ROUND(AVG(reputation)::numeric,2) AS avg_reputation,
  ROUND(AVG(badge_count)::numeric,2) AS avg_badges,

    MAX(series_size_bytes) OVER (PARTITION BY patient_id) AS max_series_size_bytes, -- not used but harmless
    SUM(series_size_bytes) AS total_size_bytes_all_series,
    COUNT(DISTINCT series_instance_uid) AS series_count,
    -- collect distinct slice intervals and exposures across all series for this patient
    ARRAY_AGG(DISTINCT si.value::FLOAT) AS patient_slice_intervals,
    ARRAY_AGG(DISTINCT ex.value::FLOAT) AS patient_exposures

WITH base AS (
  SELECT
    "date" AS date,
    "category" AS category,
    "category_name" AS category_name,
    "volume_sold_liters" AS volume_sold_liters
  FROM IOWA_LIQUOR_SALES.IOWA_LIQUOR_SALES.SALES
  WHERE "date" >= '2022-01-01'
),
-- determine last fully completed month: take max date, then last day of previous month if max date is not end of month,
-- simpler: compute last_day(add_months(current_date(), -1)) to use last fully completed month relative to today
period_bounds AS (
  SELECT
    DATE_TRUNC('month', DATEADD(month, -1, CURRENT_DATE()))::date AS month_start,
    LAST_DAY(DATEADD(month, -1, CURRENT_DATE()))::date AS month_end
),
-- generate monthly buckets from 2022-01-01 to last full month
months AS (
  SELECT
    DATE_TRUNC('month', DATEADD(month, seq4(), '2022-01-01'))::date AS month_start
  FROM TABLE(GENERATOR(ROWCOUNT => 1000))
  WHERE DATE_TRUNC('month', DATEADD(month, seq4(), '2022-01-01')) <= (SELECT month_start FROM period_bounds)
),
-- monthly volumes by category
monthly_category AS (
  SELECT
    m.month_start,
    b.category,
    b.category_name,
    SUM(COALESCE(b.volume_sold_liters,0)) AS volume_liters
  FROM months m
  LEFT JOIN base b
    ON DATE_TRUNC('month', b.date) = m.month_start
  GROUP BY m.month_start, b.category, b.category_name
),
-- total monthly volume
monthly_total AS (
  SELECT
    month_start,
    SUM(volume_liters) AS total_volume_liters
  FROM monthly_category
  GROUP BY month_start
),
-- compute monthly percentage per category (0 if no record)
monthly_pct AS (
  SELECT
    mc.month_start,
    COALESCE(mc.category, '__MISSING__') AS category,
    COALESCE(mc.category_name, '__MISSING__') AS category_name,
    COALESCE(mc.volume_liters,0) AS volume_liters,
    COALESCE(mt.total_volume_liters,0) AS total_volume_liters,
    CASE WHEN COALESCE(mt.total_volume_liters,0) = 0 THEN 0
         ELSE COALESCE(mc.volume_liters,0) / mt.total_volume_liters
    END AS pct_of_month
  FROM months mc_month
  LEFT JOIN monthly_category mc
    ON mc.month_start = mc_month.month_start
  LEFT JOIN monthly_total mt
    ON mc_month.month_start = mt.month_start
  -- ensure we only include months up to last full month
  WHERE mc_month.month_start <= (SELECT month_start FROM period_bounds)
),
-- filter categories that have at least 24 months where their average monthly percent >= 0.01 over available months?
-- Interpretation: "each contributing an average of at least 1% to the monthly sales volume over at least 24 months of available data"
-- For each category, count months where pct_of_month >= 0.01, require count >= 24, and compute average pct across all months available
eligible_categories AS (
  SELECT
    category,
    category_name,
    AVG(pct_of_month) AS avg_pct,
    SUM(CASE WHEN pct_of_month >= 0.01 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS months_at_least_1pct,
    COUNT(DISTINCT month_start) AS months_available
  FROM monthly_pct
  GROUP BY category, category_name
  HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN pct_of_month >= 0.01 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) >= 24
),
-- prepare pivoted series per category: one row per category-month
series AS (
  SELECT
    mp.month_start,
    ec.category,
    ec.category_name,
    mp.pct_of_month
  FROM monthly_pct mp
  JOIN eligible_categories ec
    ON mp.category = ec.category
),
-- compute pairwise Pearson correlation between categories over the months where both have data (we use all months; pct_of_month is 0 when absent)
pairs AS (
  SELECT
    a.category AS cat_a,
    a.category_name AS cat_a_name,
    b.category AS cat_b,
    b.category_name AS cat_b_name,
    -- compute Pearson correlation: corr(x,y) = cov(x,y)/(stddev(x)*stddev(y))
    -- use aggregate formulas
    AVG(a.pct_of_month * b.pct_of_month) - AVG(a.pct_of_month)*AVG(b.pct_of_month) AS cov_xy,
    SQRT( GREATEST(0.0, AVG(a.pct_of_month * a.pct_of_month) - AVG(a.pct_of_month)*AVG(a.pct_of_month)) ) AS sigma_x,
    SQRT( GREATEST(0.0, AVG(b.pct_of_month * b.pct_of_month) - AVG(b.pct_of_month)*AVG(b.pct_of_month)) ) AS sigma_y,
    AVG(a.pct_of_month) AS avg_x,
    AVG(b.pct_of_month) AS avg_y
  FROM
    (SELECT * FROM series) a
  JOIN
    (SELECT * FROM series) b
    ON a.month_start = b.month_start
  WHERE a.category < b.category
  GROUP BY a.category, a.category_name, b.category, b.category_name
),
pairs_corr AS (
  SELECT
    cat_a,
    cat_a_name,
    cat_b,
    cat_b_name,
    CASE WHEN sigma_x = 0 OR sigma_y = 0 THEN 0
         ELSE cov_xy / (sigma_x * sigma_y)
    END AS pearson_r
  FROM pairs
)
SELECT
  cat_a AS category_code_a,
  cat_a_name AS category_name_a,
  cat_b AS category_code_b,
  cat_b_name AS category_name_b,
  pearson_r
FROM pairs_corr
ORDER BY pearson_r ASC
LIMIT 1

mut AS (
  SELECT
    "case_barcode" AS case_barcode,
    "sample_barcode_tumor" AS sample_barcode_tumor,
    "Hugo_Symbol" AS hugo_symbol,
    "Variant_Classification" AS variant_classification

    AND "Hugo_Symbol" = 'TP53'
    AND "Variant_Classification" IS NOT NULL

mut_sample AS (
  SELECT
    sample_barcode_tumor AS sample_barcode,
    variant_classification AS mutation_type
  FROM (
    SELECT
      sample_barcode_tumor,

  WHERE rn = 1

  SELECT
    e.case_barcode,
    e.sample_barcode,
    COALESCE(m.mutation_type, 'WT') AS mutation_type,

  FROM expr e

    ON e.sample_barcode = m.sample_barcode
),
filtered AS (
  -- remove null log_expression just in case
  SELECT * FROM joined WHERE log_expression IS NOT NULL
),
agg_stats AS (
  SELECT
    COUNT(*) AS total_samples,
    COUNT(DISTINCT mutation_type) AS num_groups,
    AVG(log_expression) AS grand_mean
  FROM filtered
),

  SELECT
    mutation_type,
    COUNT(*) AS n_j,
    AVG(log_expression) AS mean_j
  FROM filtered
  GROUP BY mutation_type

  SELECT
    SUM(n_j * POWER(mean_j - (SELECT grand_mean FROM agg_stats), 2)) AS ss_between,
    (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT mutation_type) FROM filtered) AS k,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM filtered) AS N

      WHEN TRY_TO_DATE("InvoiceDate",'YYYY-MM-DD') IS NOT NULL THEN TRY_TO_DATE("InvoiceDate",'YYYY-MM-DD')
      WHEN TRY_TO_DATE("InvoiceDate",'MM/DD/YYYY') IS NOT NULL THEN TRY_TO_DATE("InvoiceDate",'MM/DD/YYYY')

invoice_totals AS (
  SELECT

  FROM invoices i
  JOIN invoice_lines il ON i.invoice_id = il.invoice_id
  WHERE COALESCE(i.invoice_date_parsed, i.invoice_date) IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY 1,2
),
invoice_2013 AS (
  SELECT
    invoice_id,
    invoice_total,
    invoice_date,
    'Q' || TO_VARCHAR(CEIL(EXTRACT(month FROM invoice_date) / 3.0)) AS quarter
  FROM invoice_totals

quarter_avgs AS (

    AVG(invoice_total) AS avg_invoice_value

WITH orders AS (

invoices AS (

order_lines AS (
  SELECT
    "OrderID" AS order_id,

customers AS (

lost_orders AS (
  SELECT

  LEFT JOIN invoices i ON o.order_id = i.order_id
  LEFT JOIN order_lines ol ON o.order_id = ol.order_id
  WHERE i.order_id IS NULL

category_max AS (

  JOIN customers c ON lo.customer_id = c.customer_id

overall_avg AS (

SELECT

WITH invoices AS (
  SELECT "InvoiceID" AS invoice_id,
         TO_DATE("InvoiceDate", 'YYYY-MM-DD') AS invoice_date,
         "CustomerID" AS customer_id
  FROM WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS.WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS.SALES_INVOICES
  WHERE TRY_TO_DATE("InvoiceDate",'YYYY-MM-DD') IS NOT NULL
    AND TO_DATE("InvoiceDate",'YYYY-MM-DD') >= '2014-01-01'
    AND TO_DATE("InvoiceDate",'YYYY-MM-DD') < '2015-01-01'
),
invoice_lines AS (
  SELECT "InvoiceLineID" AS invoice_line_id,
         "InvoiceID" AS invoice_id,
         "ExtendedPrice" AS extended_price
  FROM WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS.WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS.SALES_INVOICELINES
),
invoice_monthly_customer AS (
  -- sum extended price per customer per invoice month
  SELECT i.customer_id,
         DATE_TRUNC('month', i.invoice_date) AS month,
         SUM(COALESCE(il.extended_price,0)) AS month_total
  FROM invoices i
  JOIN invoice_lines il ON il.invoice_id = i.invoice_id
  GROUP BY i.customer_id, DATE_TRUNC('month', i.invoice_date)
),
customer_months AS (
  -- ensure months with no invoices count as zero for that customer:
  -- generate all months of 2014 then left join per customer
  SELECT c.customer_id,
         m.month,
         COALESCE(imc.month_total,0) AS month_total
  FROM (
    SELECT DISTINCT "CustomerID" AS customer_id
    FROM WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS.WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS.SALES_INVOICES
    WHERE TRY_TO_DATE("InvoiceDate",'YYYY-MM-DD') IS NOT NULL
      AND TO_DATE("InvoiceDate",'YYYY-MM-DD') >= '2014-01-01'
      AND TO_DATE("InvoiceDate",'YYYY-MM-DD') < '2015-01-01'
  ) c
  CROSS JOIN (
    SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', DATE_FROM_PARTS(2014,1,1) + (seq4()*30))::DATE AS month
    FROM TABLE(GENERATOR(ROWCOUNT => 12))
  ) m
  LEFT JOIN invoice_monthly_customer imc
    ON imc.customer_id = c.customer_id AND imc.month = m.month
),
customer_avg_monthly AS (
  -- average monthly spending per customer across 12 months
  SELECT customer_id,
         AVG(month_total) AS avg_monthly
  FROM customer_months
  GROUP BY customer_id
),
ordered_avgs AS (
  SELECT avg_monthly,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY avg_monthly) AS rn,
         COUNT(*) OVER () AS cnt
  FROM customer_avg_monthly
)
SELECT AVG(avg_monthly) AS median_avg_monthly_spending
FROM ordered_avgs
WHERE rn IN (FLOOR((cnt+1)/2.0)::INT, CEIL((cnt+1)/2.0)::INT)

topics AS (

votes AS (

),
topic_stats AS (
  SELECT
    t.id AS topic_id,

    t.title AS title,
    COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN m.id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0) AS reply_count,
    COALESCE(COUNT(DISTINCT m.post_user_id),0) AS distinct_user_replies,
    COALESCE(COUNT(v.id),0) AS total_upvotes
  FROM topics t

topic_views AS (

SELECT

  ts.title AS title,

  ts.distinct_user_replies AS distinct_user_replies,
  ts.total_upvotes AS total_upvotes,
  COALESCE(tv.total_views,0) AS total_views

JOIN topics t ON t.id = ts.topic_id

distinct_pair_counts AS (

reciprocals AS (
  SELECT
    d.from_user_id,
    d.to_user_id,

    COALESCE(r.distinct_upvotes_given, 0) AS upvotes_given_back
  FROM distinct_pair_counts d

    ON d.from_user_id = r.to_user_id
   AND d.to_user_id = r.from_user_id

with_usernames AS (

  LEFT JOIN META_KAGGLE.META_KAGGLE.USERS u_to

WITH
death AS (

    "Race"                                                                AS race,

white_deaths AS (
  SELECT

  FROM death d
  JOIN icd i
    ON d.icd10_code = i.code
  WHERE d.race = 1
),
filtered_codes AS (
  SELECT
    age,
    icd10_code,
    desc_lc,
    CASE
      WHEN desc_lc LIKE '%discharge%'
       AND desc_lc NOT LIKE '%urethral discharge%'
       AND desc_lc NOT LIKE '%discharge of firework%'
       AND desc_lc NOT LIKE '%legal intervention involving firearm discharge%'
      THEN 'discharge'
      WHEN desc_lc LIKE '%vehicle%'
      THEN 'vehicle'
      ELSE NULL
    END AS category
  FROM white_deaths
),

  SELECT

    COUNT(*)::NUMBER                                     AS death_count
  FROM filtered_codes
  WHERE category IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY age, category
),
pivot_age AS (
  SELECT
    age,
    COALESCE(MAX(CASE WHEN category = 'discharge' THEN death_count END),0) AS discharge_deaths,
    COALESCE(MAX(CASE WHEN category = 'vehicle'   THEN death_count END),0) AS vehicle_deaths
  FROM agg_by_age_category

  vehicle_deaths   AS avg_deaths_vehicle,
  CASE
    WHEN vehicle_deaths = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE discharge_deaths - vehicle_deaths
  END AS absolute_difference,
  CASE
    WHEN vehicle_deaths = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE (discharge_deaths - vehicle_deaths) / vehicle_deaths
  END AS relative_difference_ratio
FROM avg_by_age
ORDER BY age

dates AS (
  SELECT

first_two_full_weeks AS (
  SELECT
    -- find Jan 1 of previous year
    DATE_TRUNC('year', prev_year_start) AS prev_year_jan1,
    -- find first Monday on or after Jan 1 (start of first full Mon-Sun week)
    CASE
      WHEN DATE_PART('dow', DATE_TRUNC('year', prev_year_start)) = 1 THEN DATE_TRUNC('year', prev_year_start)
      ELSE DATEADD(day, (9 - DATE_PART('dow', DATE_TRUNC('year', prev_year_start))) % 7, DATE_TRUNC('year', prev_year_start))

    -- fallback: if B01003_001E not present, try top-level number

  FROM acs_raw
